subtopics.name: useState
subtopics.content: The useState hook allows you to add state to functional components. It returns an array with the current state value and a function to update it. It is the most commonly used hook for managing local component state.

subtopics.name: useEffect
subtopics.content: The useEffect hook lets you perform side effects in functional components. It serves the same purpose as componentDidMount, componentDidUpdate, and componentWillUnmount in React classes, but unified into a single API.

subtopics.name: useRef
subtopics.content: The useRef hook returns a mutable ref object whose .current property is initialized to the passed argument. The returned object will persist for the full lifetime of the component. It is commonly used to access DOM elements directly.

subtopics.name: useMemo
subtopics.content: The useMemo hook returns a memoized value. It only recomputes the memoized value when one of the dependencies has changed. This optimization helps to avoid expensive calculations on every render.

subtopics.name: useCallback
subtopics.content: The useCallback hook returns a memoized version of the callback that only changes if one of the dependencies has changed. This is useful when passing callbacks to optimized child components that rely on reference equality to prevent unnecessary renders.

subtopics.name: Custom Hooks
subtopics.content: Custom hooks allow you to extract component logic into reusable functions. A custom hook is a JavaScript function whose name starts with 'use' and that may call other hooks. This helps in sharing logic between multiple components.

subtopics.name: Lifecycle Basics
subtopics.content: Every React component goes through a lifecycle of events: Mounting (being put into the DOM), Updating (when props or state change), and Unmounting (being removed from the DOM). Hooks provide a way to hook into these events in functional components.

subtopics.name: Side Effects
subtopics.content: Side effects include data fetching, setting up a subscription, and manually changing the DOM in React components. These should be handled within the useEffect hook to ensure the UI stays consistent and performance is maintained.
